payload.task_text:
Our investment team needs to compile the weekly market analysis report. A financial analytics dashboard is available at http://localhost:30204/dashboard.html that displays sector performance indices, weekly returns, year-to-date returns, volatility levels, and analyst consensus ratings for five market sectors: Communication Services, Consumer Cyclical, Financial Services, Healthcare, and Energy.

We also track five individual stocks that represent these sectors: GOOGL for Communication Services, AMZN for Consumer Cyclical, JPM for Financial Services, JNJ for Healthcare, and XOM for Energy. We need to cross-reference sector-level performance with individual stock data.

Please browse the market dashboard and extract all sector performance data including weekly return, sector index value, YTD return, volatility level, analyst consensus rating, and target price upside for each of the five sectors.

Then retrieve the current stock data for each of the five tickers (GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM) from the financial data service. For each stock, get the current price, sector, market capitalization, P/E ratio, and dividend yield.

Create a Google Sheet called "Weekly_Market_Analysis" with two sheets. The first sheet called "Sector Performance" should have columns Sector, Weekly_Return, Sector_Index, YTD_Return, Volatility, Consensus, and Target_Upside, with one row for each of the five sectors. The second sheet called "Stock vs Sector" should have columns Ticker, Stock_Price, Sector, Market_Cap_B (market cap in billions, rounded to 1 decimal), PE_Ratio, Dividend_Yield_Pct, Sector_Weekly_Return, and Sector_YTD_Return. Map each stock to its corresponding sector data from the dashboard.

Next, create a Word document called "Weekly_Market_Report.docx" in the workspace as an executive summary. Include a title, a market overview paragraph, a section for each sector discussing the sector index performance alongside the representative stock, and a conclusion identifying the best and worst performing sectors of the week ranked by weekly return (the sector with the highest weekly return is the best; the sector with the lowest weekly return is the worst, even if it is positive).

Finally, send an email to committee@investmentfirm.com with the subject "Weekly Market Analysis Report" (the sender address is fixed by the email environment, so just use your default account). The body should highlight the top performing sector and any sectors with negative weekly returns.

Save all output files to the workspace directory.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent; do not dispatch sub-agents. The stock calls are tiny, while delegated browser work adds no useful dependency. First freeze the task-visible agent-workspace absolute path from the Visible Boundary/current working directory; never assume `/workspace`.

In one orchestration response, call `mcp__playwright_with_chunk__browser_navigate` exactly once for `http://localhost:30204/dashboard.html` and issue the five Yahoo Finance stock-info calls for `GOOGL`, `AMZN`, `JPM`, `JNJ`, and `XOM` natively in parallel. If navigation succeeds, call `browser_snapshot` exactly once and extract the five named sector rows. Do not call `browser_install`, Terminal, PDF, Word-browser helpers, email-browser helpers, alternate URLs, or any unrelated tool while acquiring sources; on a navigation/snapshot failure, report the exact source blocker and do not guess dashboard values.

Require exactly five complete sector rows `{sector,weekly_return,sector_index,ytd_return,volatility,consensus,target_upside}` and five complete stock rows `{ticker,current_price,sector,market_cap,pe_ratio,dividend_yield}`. Freeze one literal canonical five-row stock-sector join, including raw-return best/worst sectors and market cap converted to billions once. From only that payload, the main agent creates exactly one `Weekly_Market_Analysis` Google spreadsheet and `<agent_workspace>/Weekly_Market_Report.docx`, using the task's exact sheets, columns, sections, mapping, and rounding, and sends one email to `committee@investmentfirm.com` with subject `Weekly Market Analysis Report`. Read each output once and reconcile it to the same payload; do not add sent-mail discovery, browser retries, diagnostic writes, or a verification wave.

nodes.text:
You are gathering current stock data from Yahoo Finance for a weekly market analysis report. Use the tool `mcp__yahoo-finance__get_stock_info` (one call per ticker) for these five tickers: GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM.

For each ticker extract:
1. Current price (field `currentPrice` or `regularMarketPrice`)
2. Sector (field `sector`)
3. Market capitalization (field `marketCap`, raw value in dollars)
4. Trailing P/E ratio (field `trailingPE`)
5. Dividend yield: report the raw `dividendYield` field value, plus `trailingAnnualDividendRate` (or `dividendRate`) and the current price, so the yield can be cross-checked as (dividendRate / price * 100).

Then return a COMPACT report — exactly one line per ticker, no raw dumps, no extra commentary — in this exact format:

TICKER: price=<X> | sector=<sector string> | marketCap=<raw dollars> | marketCapB=<raw/1e9 rounded to 1 decimal> | PE=<X> | dividendYield_raw=<raw field value or N/A> | divRate=<rate or 0> | divYieldPct=<dividendRate/price*100 rounded to 2 decimals, or 0 if no dividend>

Rules:
- If a field is missing or None, write N/A for it.
- AMZN typically pays no dividend — yield should be 0.
- marketCapB must be marketCap divided by 1,000,000,000, rounded to 1 decimal place.
- Do not modify anything; this is read-only data gathering.
Fetch stock data from Yahoo Finance

Create a Microsoft Word executive summary report at this EXACT absolute path (do not use any other location):

/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3-Flash/SingleUserTurn-playwright-yf-market-dashboard-gsheet-word/workspace/Weekly_Market_Report.docx

Use the `mcp__word__*` tools (create_document, add_heading, add_paragraph, add_table, format_table/highlight_table_header/apply_table_alternating_rows as available). Create the document with title metadata "Weekly Market Analysis Report". Build the document with EXACTLY this structure and content (use the text verbatim):

1. Heading level 1: "Weekly Market Analysis Report"
2. Paragraph (italic): "Report Period: March 1-7, 2026 | Data Sources: Market Analytics Pro Sector Dashboard; Yahoo Finance"
3. Heading level 2: "Market Overview"
4. Paragraph: "In the week of March 1-7, 2026, four of the five tracked market sectors posted positive weekly returns. Energy led all groups at +3.1%, followed closely by Communication Services at +2.8%, while Financial Services added +1.5% and Healthcare edged up +0.3%. Consumer Cyclical was the lone decliner at -1.2%. Year to date, Energy (+15.2%) and Communication Services (+12.4%) hold the strongest gains, whereas Healthcare remains the only sector in negative territory at -2.1%. Volatility is rated High in both Energy and Communication Services, and analyst sentiment is most bullish on those two groups, both carrying Strong Buy consensus ratings with average target price upside of +22.1% and +18.5% respectively. Cross-referencing each sector with its representative stock (GOOGL, AMZN, JPM, JNJ, XOM) confirms that individual large-cap names are broadly tracking their sector-level trends."
5. A 6-row by 7-column summary table. Header row: "Sector", "Weekly Return", "Sector Index", "YTD Return", "Volatility", "Consensus", "Target Upside". Data rows in this order:
   - "Communication Services", "+2.8%", "118.5", "+12.4%", "High", "Strong Buy", "+18.5%"
   - "Consumer Cyclical", "-1.2%", "105.3", "+5.7%", "Medium", "Buy", "+12.3%"
   - "Financial Services", "+1.5%", "112.8", "+8.9%", "Medium", "Buy", "+9.8%"
   - "Healthcare", "+0.3%", "98.7", "-2.1%", "Low", "Hold", "+5.2%"
   - "Energy", "+3.1%", "122.4", "+15.2%", "High", "Strong Buy", "+22.1%"
   Format the table so the header row is highlighted (e.g. highlight_table_header) and, if the tool is available, apply alternating row colors.
6. Heading level 2: "Communication Services (Representative Stock: GOOGL - Alphabet)"
7. Paragraph: "Communication Services gained +2.8% on the week with the sector index at 118.5, and it is up +12.4% year to date. Volatility is rated High, analysts hold a Strong Buy consensus, and the average target price upside is +18.5%. Alphabet (GOOGL) trades at $300.88 with a market capitalization of $3,639.7 billion, a trailing P/E of 27.81, and a dividend yield of 0.28%. GOOGL's momentum mirrors the sector's leadership position, though its premium valuation leaves it sensitive to shifts in advertising and AI-related spending expectations."
8. Heading level 2: "Consumer Cyclical (Representative Stock: AMZN - Amazon)"
9. Paragraph: "Consumer Cyclical was the weakest sector of the week, slipping -1.2% with the sector index at 105.3; it is still +5.7% year to date. Volatility is rated Medium, the consensus is Buy, and average target price upside is +12.3%. Amazon (AMZN) trades at $218.94 with a market capitalization of $2,350.3 billion and a trailing P/E of 30.49; AMZN pays no dividend (0.00% yield). The pullback leaves Consumer Cyclical as the only sector with a negative weekly return, reflecting softness in discretionary-spending sentiment."
10. Heading level 2: "Financial Services (Representative Stock: JPM - JPMorgan Chase)"
11. Paragraph: "Financial Services rose +1.5% on the week with the sector index at 112.8, and it is +8.9% year to date. Volatility is rated Medium, the consensus is Buy, and average target price upside is +9.8%. JPMorgan Chase (JPM) trades at $293.55 with a market capitalization of $791.7 billion, a trailing P/E of 14.66, and a dividend yield of 2.00%. JPM's modest valuation and solid yield make it a core holding as the sector continues its steady climb."
12. Heading level 2: "Healthcare (Representative Stock: JNJ - Johnson & Johnson)"
13. Paragraph: "Healthcare eked out a +0.3% weekly gain with the sector index at 98.7, but it remains the only sector negative year to date at -2.1%. Volatility is rated Low, the consensus is Hold - the most cautious rating on the dashboard - and average target price upside is +5.2%. Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) trades at $239.63 with a market capitalization of $577.5 billion, a trailing P/E of 21.71, and a dividend yield of 2.12%. The group's defensive characteristics keep volatility low, but it currently lacks near-term catalysts."
14. Heading level 2: "Energy (Representative Stock: XOM - Exxon Mobil)"
15. Paragraph: "Energy was the top performer of the week, up +3.1%, with the sector index at 122.4 - the highest index level among the five groups - and it leads year-to-date performance at +15.2%. Volatility is rated High, the consensus is Strong Buy, and average target price upside is the largest on the board at +22.1%. Exxon Mobil (XOM) trades at $150.76 with a market capitalization of $628.2 billion, a trailing P/E of 22.50, and a dividend yield of 2.75%, the richest yield among the five representative stocks."
16. Heading level 2: "Conclusion"
17. Paragraph: "Ranked by weekly return, the best performing sector of the week was Energy at +3.1%, supported by the highest sector index (122.4), a Strong Buy consensus, and the largest average target price upside (+22.1%). The worst performing sector of the week was Consumer Cyclical at -1.2% - the only sector with a negative weekly return - despite retaining a Buy consensus and remaining +5.7% year to date."
18. Paragraph: "Full weekly ranking by weekly return: 1) Energy +3.1%; 2) Communication Services +2.8%; 3) Financial Services +1.5%; 4) Healthcare +0.3%; 5) Consumer Cyclical -1.2%. The committee should also note that Healthcare remains the only sector negative year to date (-2.1%) and carries the board's only Hold rating, while the divergence between commodity-led strength in Energy and discretionary weakness in Consumer Cyclical is the key sector-rotation signal of the week."

After building, verify with get_document_info (and get_document_text if needed) that the file exists at the exact path, contains all 7 headings (title + Market Overview + 5 sector headings + Conclusion... i.e. 8 headings total), the 6x7 table, and all paragraphs. Report back: the final absolute file path, file size, number of paragraphs/tables, and confirmation that every required section is present. Do not create any other files.
Build Word executive summary report
